summary.headline: Nanta Tech H1 FY27 revenue rose 97.7% YoY to INR42.6 crore, with EBITDA margin at 23.3% and PAT at INR5.1 crore.
summary.overview: Nanta Tech reported H1 FY27 revenue from operations of about INR42.6 crore (up 97.7% YoY from INR21.5 crore), EBITDA of INR9.9 crore (up 221.2%) and PAT of INR5.1 crore (up 131.4%). Management attributed the margin expansion to a rising mix of higher-margin robotics and AI versus audio-video. During the half it signed a Connplex LoI, an Aimtron EMS manufacturing MoU, a GM Biovalley MoU for Southern Asia, and set up a UAE subsidiary. On the call, management raised its FY27 growth view to 45-50% from the earlier 30% guidance, but gave no formal revised figure.

financial_highlights.change: +97.7% YoY vs INR21.5 crore in H1 FY26
vs 10.2% in H1 FY26 (stated as +170 points)

financial_highlights.metric: Robotics and AI order book (end H1)

segments.name: Robotics and AI (Allbotix brand, RSVP software)
segments.commentary: Higher-margin vertical per management; serves hospitality, healthcare, logistics, warehousing, cleaning. Around 200 robots deployed in H1, with 800-plus targeted in H2 against a FY27 target of at least 1,000. Outright sales about 50% and service/RaaS about 50% of robot business.

segments.name: Audio-video integration
segments.commentary: Lower-margin vertical per management; end-to-end AV design, supply, installation and maintenance for enterprise, government and institutional clients. No segment revenue or margin split was given on the call; management said a robotics vs AI revenue breakup would be provided later.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth: asked whether guidance (earlier 30%, with 40-50% previously discussed) would be raised, management said it expects 45-50% growth this year.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 20-22% for the full year, versus 23.3% in H1.
FY27 target of at least 1,000 robot deployments, with about 800-plus planned in H2.

FY28: management has not set a deployment target; said FY27 growth of 40-50% can be sustained and possibly exceeded. It did not reconfirm the INR200 crore FY28 revenue figure cited by an analyst from the March 2026 call.
Robotics EBITDA is expected to rise in mix terms; capex-model deployments run about 30-35% EBITDA, AMC is about 12-20% of the hardware/software price from year two.
capex_capacity: No in-house robot manufacturing today; Aimtron (EMS partner) will manufacture existing orders, with an indicative INR10 crore over 15 months.
In-house assembly line targeted before end of CY2026; capex not finalised, in initial phase, to cover new H2 models and best-selling models.
Deployment cycle from order to client site is about 60-90 days, with a plan to shorten it.
RaaS: about 25-30% of robot deployments expected in FY27; management is working out how to fund the higher capex needed for a larger RaaS push.
Experience centres opened in Ahmedabad (flagship) and Mumbai (Andheri East).
demand_pricing: Pipeline of large fleet requests (50-200 robots per client) is moving from POC to implementation, with several clients asking for RaaS.
Connplex Cinemas LoI: 100 AT10 robots under a RaaS model, indicative INR14.4 crore over 36 months.
Pointer Insurance AI automation order of INR6.6 crore over 6 months, marking entry into BFSI.
Recurring base: about 400 robots sold, expected to move into AMC from year-end; about 10+ active SaaS clients.
Competition: few Indian players, with new entrants appearing each quarter. Management says end-to-end integration with client systems is the main barrier to entry.

Defence: first direct defence order is a pilot Phase 1 (value not disclosed, below the exchange-disclosure threshold per management), with a prototype due by end-December and a larger order expected in the last quarter of H2.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth guidance be raised from the earlier 40-50% view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is comfortable with 30% and expects 45-50% growth for FY27, supported by the order book and international pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin improvement and what is the full-year margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix shift toward robotics and AI, which is higher margin than AV. Full-year EBITDA margin expected at 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: How many robots were deployed in H1 and what is the split by use case and sales model?
qa_highlights.answer: About 200 robots deployed in H1 and 800-plus planned for H2; mostly autonomous cleaning robots on factory floors and corporate offices. Outright sales about 50%, service model about 50%, with more outright sales expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and is the FY28 INR200 crore revenue view still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Robotics and AI order book is about INR60 crore at end H1. Management said growth of 45-50% this year and at least a similar rate next year, with margins expected to improve. It did not restate the INR200 crore figure.

qa_highlights.question: What proprietary IP is owned versus outsourced, and what drives robot margins?
qa_highlights.answer: About 17 in-house robot models; in-house ROS 2 OS, MeetIQ, VisitIQ and NTra software, with source code held on in-house servers and offered as SaaS. Hardware is first-year bundled with software, followed by AMC.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the recurring base and what are the margins on AMC and RaaS?
qa_highlights.answer: About 400 robots will move into AMC before year-end; more than 10 SaaS clients. AMC is about 12-20% from year two. Capex deployments earn about 30-35% EBITDA; RaaS deals have a 15-16 month payback and 24-48 month contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the binding status of MoUs and LoIs, and what is the local value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Most are at implementation or POC stage, with 14-24 month contracts. Motors and actuators (three to four components) are still imported from China and Taiwan, while the rest is sourced in India.

risks_watch: Rising RaaS mix requires large upfront capex and funding; RaaS payback is about 15-16 months and contracts run 24-48 months.
Robot manufacturing is outsourced to Aimtron for now; the in-house assembly line is not yet funded or commissioned.
Heavy H2 weighting: 800-plus of the 1,000 robot target and the defence order are both due in H2.
Management declined to set an FY28 deployment target and did not reconfirm the prior INR200 crore FY28 revenue figure.
Revenue and margin breakup between robotics/AI and AV was not disclosed on the call; management said it would be provided.
Key motors and actuators depend on China and Taiwan imports.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, with 45-50% FY27 growth and a 1,000-robot target stated firmly. Less specific on FY28 scale, funding for RaaS, and the revenue split, where management deferred or said it would provide details later.
key_quotes: So, we are very confident that we will able to deliver 45% to 50% growth in this year.
So, our EBITDA margin would be around 20% that we are expecting that will be there, between 20% to 22% our EBITDA margin will be there.
We have not put a target in FY28. We are just looking forward to complete our FY27 target aggressively.

adds.what: In-house robot assembly line (capex not finalised, initial phase; targeted before end of CY2026)
Aimtron EMS outsourced manufacturing of existing robot orders (indicative INR10 crore over 15 months)

growth.why: Management expects FY27 revenue growth of 45-50% (midpoint 47.5%, raised from 30%), backed by about INR60 crore robotics order book, a Connplex RaaS LoI (INR14.4 crore) and a target of 1,000+ robot deployments, though in-house manufacturing capex is not finalised and robot assembly is outsourced to Aimtron.
